# Specialize this scaffold into a portfolio

You are looking at **solorepo**, a scaffold for building software products as a
team of one in the agentic AI era. Specializing it produces a **Portfolio**:
one repo, one Bounded Context, one Ubiquitous Language, holding however many
Products and Projects.

Turning this scaffold into a new portfolio repo. Done once, by an agent following these steps, and never again in that repo.

**Where the judgement is.** Which of the inherited terms this portfolio actually needs, who its stakeholders really are, and what its domain calls things. None of it is derivable from the scaffold, which is why this is a procedure to follow rather than a program to run.

## Steps

1. **Start a new empty repo.** Copy only what the steps below name — never clone, and never copy the whole tree: a clone carries the scaffold's commit history and an `origin` pointing back at it, and neither belongs to a portfolio.
2. **Copy what is inherited.** Copy what is inherited — `.meta/work/`, `.meta/ddd/`, `.meta/work_ontology.yaml`, `.meta/ddd_ontology.yaml`, `.meta/render.py`, `.meta/check.py`, `.meta/check_pr.py`, `.meta/lib/` (solorepo's DR-217), `.meta/apm_compile.py`, `.meta/agents.py` (solorepo's DR-191), `.meta/dereference.py`, `.meta/depth.py` (solorepo's DR-188), `.meta/gate`, `.meta/next.py`, `.meta/search.py` (solorepo's DR-194), `.meta/timing.py`, `.meta/wikisplain.py` (solorepo's DR-187), `.meta/terms.py` (solorepo's DR-234), `.meta/bootstrap.py` (solorepo's DR-206), `.meta/ruff.toml`, `.meta/mypy.ini`, `.meta/actions/`, `.meta/say/`, `.meta/hooks/`, `.meta/checks/`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.meta/assertions/imported/`, `.meta/.apm/`, `.meta/principles.md`, `.meta/schemas.md`, `.meta/templates/`, `.meta/arc/Dockerfile`, `.github/workflows/coder.yml`, `.github/workflows/review.yml`, `.meta/detect_fallback.py` (solorepo's DR-245), `.meta/run_agy.py` (solorepo's DR-257), `.github/workflows/triage.yml` (solorepo's DR-230), `.github/workflows/merge.yml`, `.github/workflows/advance.yml`, `.github/workflows/reconcile.yml` (solorepo's DR-264), `wiki/solorepo/` (solorepo's DR-184), `stakeholders/` and `.gitignore`. The channel, its hooks and the settings that register them travel with the loop workflows rather than after them: every instruction those six give is typed as a program of `.meta/say/`, most of `check.py`'s 62 prechecks load the channel or a hook, and `.claude/settings.json` is the one place the hook is invoked and the unsigned `gh` verbs denied (DR-069) — a hook file that nothing invokes is the channel as a rule to remember, which is what it exists not to be. The schemas and the channel stay in this copy set rather than riding inside APM skills (DR-173). A portfolio without them has a coder that cannot commit, a gate that cannot run its own first steps, and a channel nothing enforces. The Gemini fallback (`.meta/detect_fallback.py`) travels with `coder.yml`, `review.yml`, and `triage.yml`: it defaults to disabled (`'false'`) to prevent unauthenticated execution failures in portfolios lacking local ARC credential infrastructure (solorepo's DR-245), and setting repository variable `vars.GEMINI_FALLBACK` to `'true'` activates fallback to containerized Antigravity CLI (`agy`) under personal subscription quota (solorepo's DR-245, solorepo's #669). Not the generated pages, and not the two Issue forms or the pull request form; Specialization's *Render and check* step writes all of those from the templates. Not the gate workflow either: solorepo's runs the Bootstrap seeds, which a portfolio has not got, and Specialization's *Copy template replacements and link agents* step writes a portfolio's own, whose one gate job runs `.meta/gate` over the Projects its assertions declare (DR-115). Then retarget `runs-on:` in every workflow this step copies: each of them names `arc-runner-set`, a self-hosted scale set that exists on the scaffold's own machine (DR-137, DR-140), and none of what stands one up is copied. A job whose label no runner offers does not fail — it queues, so the loops never start and an armed merge goes behind with nobody left to notice (#93), which is quieter than a job that goes red. `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` with `container: ghcr.io/caindy/solorepo-runner:2.337.0-4` is the answer unless this portfolio stands up a scale set of its own (DR-160). The image is public on GHCR so workflows pull without credentials, pre-bakes the single-source CLI toolchain (solorepo's DR-160) alongside Python 3.13 as default `python3` (solorepo's DR-268), and `.meta/arc/Dockerfile` copied above gives the portfolio the recipe to rebuild, customize, or bump the image.
3. **Copy template replacements and link agents.** Copy every file under `template/` to its matching path, then link `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` to `AGENTS.md`. These are the replacements: the files that must carry none of the scaffold's content.
4. **Fill placeholders and write assertions.** Fill in every placeholder, and write the portfolio's own assertions — its Portfolio, Products and Projects; its Personas, once there is research to draw them from; its Bounded Context and the words its domain experts actually use. When asserting Projects in `assertions/structure.yaml`, optionally declare `critical_paths` (globs for security boundaries, public contracts, or migrations) to route changes on them to deep reviewer auditing under the 4-layer template method pipeline (solorepo's DR-188). If the portfolio requires dynamic heuristics (such as AST inspections, complexity thresholds, or sensitive metadata), provide an executable hook at `.meta/hooks/depth.py` implementing `evaluate_depth(pr_meta, files, diff_patch)` (an annotated example sits at `.meta/hooks/depth.py.example`).
5. **Choose languages and bootstrap.** Choose the languages the portfolio will use, from those solorepo's `bootstraps/` supports, and bring them to hand: running `just bootstrap <lang> <path>` instantiates a seed project and registers it in `assertions/structure.yaml` (solorepo's DR-206). Language adoption can happen now or be deferred to any point in the portfolio lifecycle.
6. **Render and check.** Re-render, then run the gate. It fails on any placeholder left behind, so run it before removing anything. Both green before going on.
7. **Confirm scaffold-only paths absent.** Confirm `SPECIALIZE.md` and `template/` are absent. A portfolio specializes nothing, and leaving either invites someone to run this twice.
8. **Commit.** All changes verified, commit the specialized repository under the author's own credential.

_Produces: A portfolio repo, with its own history and nothing of the scaffold's._
